theory.intro: The triangle area formula $A = \tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ can be rearranged to find an unknown side or included angle when the area is known. Solving for an angle gives two supplementary solutions: an acute angle $C$ and an obtuse angle $180^{\circ} - C$.
facts: To find an unknown side length, rearrange the area formula to $b = \dfrac{2A}{a\sin C}$.
To find the included angle, rearrange the area formula to $\sin C = \dfrac{2A}{ab}$.
Because $\sin C = \sin(180^{\circ} - C)$, there are two supplementary angle solutions: acute $C$ and obtuse $180^{\circ} - C$.
If the question specifies whether the triangle is acute or obtuse, give only that single angle.
If no angle type is specified, both the acute and obtuse angles are valid solutions and must be stated.
For an isosceles triangle with equal sides $x$ and included angle $C$, each side is $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{2A}{\sin C}}$.
steps: Substitute the known area, side lengths, and angle
Rearrange and solve for the unknown side or angle
State the acute or obtuse solution, or both if unrestricted

foundation.question_text: A triangle has an area of $36\text{ cm}^{2}$, a side of length $9\text{ cm}$, and an included angle of $30^{\circ}$. Find the length of the other side forming this angle.

A triangle has an area of $42\text{ m}^{2}$. Two of its sides meet at an obtuse angle of $120^{\circ}$, and one of those sides is $14\text{ m}$ long. Find the length of the other side, correct to $1$ decimal place.
A triangle has sides of $8\text{ cm}$ and $11\text{ cm}$ and an area of $22\text{ cm}^{2}$. Given that the included angle $\theta$ is acute, find $\theta$ to the nearest degree.
A triangle has sides of length $6\text{ m}$ and $10\text{ m}$ and an area of $15\text{ m}^{2}$. Given that the included angle $\theta$ is obtuse, find $\theta$ to the nearest degree.
A triangle has sides of $7\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ and an area of $35\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find both possible sizes of the included angle $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

development.question_text: A triangular solar panel has an area of $1.8\text{ m}^{2}$. One edge is $2.4\text{ m}$ long and makes an angle of $52^{\circ}$ with an adjacent edge. Find the length of the adjacent edge, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A triangular roof gable has an area of $15.6\text{ m}^{2}$. Two timber rafters meet at an obtuse ridge angle of $118^{\circ}$. If one rafter is $5.8\text{ m}$ long, calculate the length of the other rafter, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A surveyor notes that two straight boundaries of a triangular plot measure $45\text{ m}$ and $60\text{ m}$, enclosing an area of $1050\text{ m}^{2}$. Find both possible values for the angle between these two boundaries, correct to $1$ decimal place.
An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of $40^{\circ}$ and an area of $50\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find the length of each of the two equal sides, correct to $2$ decimal places.

mastery.question_text: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles of $72^{\circ}$ and an area of $84\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find the length of each of the two equal sides, correct to $2$ decimal places.
A triangle has sides of length $4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$ and $6\text{ cm}$, and its area is $18\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find the two exact possible values for the included angle $\theta$ in degrees.

In triangle $ABC$, the ratio of side lengths $a : b$ is $3 : 4$, the included angle $C$ is $45^{\circ}$, and the area of the triangle is $54\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find the exact length of the shorter side $a$.
